name: jcode-vscode
description: Full Jcode agent wrapper: sidebar chat, editor context, session management, and slash commands over the official jcode SDK (api-bridge).

jcode.launchArguments.description: Extra global arguments passed to Jcode chat runs and the interactive terminal.

jcode.maxSelectionCharacters.description: Maximum number of selected characters that may be sent to Jcode.

jcode.contextWindowTokens.markdownDescription: Override the context window used by the sidebar occupancy meter. `0` uses Jcode's model-family defaults (normally 200K, with known long-context models detected automatically).

jcode.defaultModel.markdownDescription: Default model applied to new Jcode chat sessions and the terminal agent, e.g. `deepseek-v4-pro`. When empty, Jcode's own default model is used. The sidebar chat has its own model picker that overrides this.

jcode.models.markdownDescription: Fallback model names for the sidebar chat model picker when Jcode's live model catalog is unreachable. When empty, a built-in curated list is used. The picker normally lists the real catalog from the connected Jcode daemon (`listModels`).

jcode.apiSocketPath.markdownDescription: Override the harness API socket path used by the sidebar chat. Leave empty for the default (extension storage, or the `JCODE_API_SOCKET` environment variable when set).

jcode.autoApprove.markdownDescription: Automatically allow permission prompts issued by the agent. When disabled, permission requests surface in the chat for you to approve or deny. (The current api-bridge does not yet advertise the `permissions` capability, so this is a no-op until it does.)

jcode.shareEditorContext.markdownDescription: Include a compact summary of the active editor, selection, and open files with each sidebar message so the agent knows what you are looking at in VS Code.

jcode.defaultEffort.markdownDescription: Default reasoning effort applied to new Jcode chat sessions (`setReasoningEffort`) and passed to the terminal agent via the `JCODE_OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT` / `JCODE_ANTHROPIC_REASONING_EFFORT` environment variables. When empty, Jcode's own default is used. Levels: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; the accepted set depends on the provider.
